image.name: DataBank
image.description: DataBank Holdings, Ltd. operates a nationwide digital-infrastructure platform providing colocation, interconnection, cloud, storage, managed security and compliance services to enterprise, cloud, content and technology customers. Founded in Dallas in 2005, DataBank was acquired from Avista by a DigitalBridge-led group in July 2016 and has since expanded through acquisitions, development and multiple recapitalizations. DataBank reported more than 70 data centers in more than 25 markets, 20 interconnection hubs, more than 2,200 customers and more than $1 billion of revenue in May 2026. The current manager-universe ownership roster is DigitalBridge, Swiss Life Asset Managers, IMCO, AustralianSuper, Northleaf Capital Partners, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management. DigitalBridge disclosed a 7.8% continuing stake after the January 2025 secondary. TIAA's Real Estate Account separately disclosed a 14.8% beneficial stake through DigitalBridge Zeus vehicles; DataBank brands that relationship as Nuveen, but it is not evidenced as a Nuveen Infrastructure investment. EDF Invest and TJC are also current investors outside the supplied manager universe. Individual data centers, campuses, interconnection hubs and acquired operating assets remain within the single DataBank platform boundary. No later full sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

milestones.event: DataBank Ltd. was founded in the former Federal Reserve Bank Building in downtown Dallas, Texas.
Digital Bridge acquired DataBank from Avista Capital Partners with TIAA, Allstate Investments and The Edgewater Funds, launching its first data-center platform.

Colony Capital purchased $185 million of secondary DataBank interests from Edgewater and Allstate; Edgewater exited, Allstate retained half of its prior interest and the Nuveen-branded TIAA investment continued.

A Swiss Life-led consortium with EDF Invest, Northleaf and Ardian closed a collective 35% DataBank interest for approximately $1.5 billion; IMCO then agreed to invest up to $450 million in the continuing recapitalization.

DataBank announced an approximately $2.0 billion equity raise led by AustralianSuper's $1.5 billion commitment, which would make AustralianSuper a significant minority owner; DataBank now lists it as a current investor.

DataBank announced a $250 million TJC investment and an approximately $600 million secondary share sale; DigitalBridge disclosed that the transaction would adjust its continuing DataBank stake to 7.8%.
